outcome: sulprostone failure (defined as the need for one or more invasive procedures: intrauterine balloon tamponade, arterial embolisation, conservative surgery, or hysterectomy)
cohort: The cohort consisted of women aged 18 years or older, with a gestational age of 26-42 weeks, who experienced postpartum haemorrhage after vaginal delivery and received sulprostone treatment between January 2019 and December 2020.
finding: Sulprostone failure in the management of postpartum haemorrhage after vaginal delivery was independently associated with previous caesarean section, episiotomy, history of PPH, and a higher shock index at sulprostone administration.
mod_finding: Previous caesarean section and episiotomy were independently associated with an increased risk of sulprostone failure in women experiencing PPH after vaginal delivery.
